## Parent

#68

## What to build

Preserve TCP interoperability with iroh-tunnel 0.4 where feasible, without introducing a wire-version negotiation framework.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test real 0.4 Access → redesigned Serve and redesigned Access → real 0.4 Serve against a TCP target; record exact versions and outcomes.
- [ ] If either path fails, document the compatibility trade-off and obtain the user's decision before a breaking release; do not silently declare compatibility.
- [ ] Do not add a version-negotiation framework for this redesign. Test other supported peer combinations as applicable.

## Traceability

TC-02; AC-TC-02; story 16. The compatibility test is not yet performed. Refer to #68 and the resolution of #75.

## Blocked by

Native issue dependencies are authoritative. Real executable end-to-end evidence is required; disclose unavailable environments.

comments.body:
## Readiness and supporting artifacts · audit 2026

Shared rule/acceptance reference: https://github.com/naicoi92/iroh-tunnel/issues/68#issuecomment-6489433346

Confirmed: incompatible peers fail clearly without silent downgrade. Wire version negotiation is open.

Open native blockers at audit: none. Live dependency status is authoritative. Issue acceptance criteria must be met and relevant real-path or platform evidence recorded before closure. Local design diagrams are not yet published and are not claimed as GitHub-accessible evidence.

## Partial decision — user confirmed

Wire protocol version is independent of binary release version. Peers with compatible wire versions may interoperate; incompatible versions fail clearly without silent downgrade. Exact negotiation, version compatibility rules and acceptance details remain open. Do not close this issue yet.

## Supersession and 0.4 compatibility clarification

The earlier partial suggestion to introduce an independent wire-version framework is superseded: the user does not want expanded version checking or negotiation in this redesign and expects existing 0.4 connections not to break. Existing repository protocol documentation describes service ALPN without version negotiation; this is not evidence that redesigned peers interoperate. Verify old Access → new Serve and new Access → old Serve with actual 0.4 artifacts and report any compatibility limits. Exact scope remains open; do not close this issue or implement a new negotiation framework by assumption.

## Partial decision — user confirmed

Preserve TCP compatibility with 0.4 where feasible. Test both 0.4 Access → redesigned Serve and redesigned Access → 0.4 Serve. If either fails, report the trade-off for user decision; compatibility is not an unconditional release gate. Do not add a version-negotiation framework for this redesign. The compatibility test has not run.

## Resolution — supersedes original acceptance wording

User decided not to introduce a wire-version negotiation framework. Seek TCP interoperability with iroh-tunnel 0.4 where feasible; test both old Access → new Serve and new Access → old Serve, and present any failure for user decision before a breaking release. Exact test results are implementation evidence tracked by #85, not a condition for closing this decision issue. This supersedes the original request to design negotiation/version evolution.
